questions.stem: In Perlas grading, how does the antrum look in grade 0 (low risk)?
options: Empty, small and collapsed in both positions

questions.stem: Which transducer gives adequate depth for gastric ultrasound in adults?
questions.answer: A low-frequency curved array transducer (2–5 MHz)

questions.stem: When may a high-frequency linear transducer be used for gastric ultrasound?
questions.answer: In paediatric or very lean patients

questions.stem: In which plane and region is the gastric antrum scanned?
questions.answer: Sagittal or parasagittal plane in the epigastrium

questions.stem: Which structures lie posterior to the gastric antrum?
questions.answer: The pancreas and the abdominal aorta/inferior vena cava

questions.stem: What lies anterior to the gastric antrum on ultrasound?
questions.answer: The left lobe of the liver

questions.stem: Which positions should be imaged in gastric ultrasound?
questions.answer: Both supine and right lateral decubitus (RLD)

questions.stem: Why is the RLD position used in gastric ultrasound?
questions.answer: It shifts gastric contents into the antrum, maximising sensitivity for low-volume fluid or hidden solids
